role.altitude: The remote sensing technician keeps judging image quality, designing databases and matching sensors to project needs; hand-run corrections, retyping flight logs and writing layer metadata shrink.
reach: Scientists and planners who use the data
skills_to_grow: Building and maintaining batch processing chains and register scripts
role.ambitious_version: A technician whose corrected imagery and records are ready the day after a flight, with every step logged.

tasks.short: Get raw imagery and sensor data, correct raw data for errors due to skew or atmospheric variation, check the corrected images against reference points and log the corrections applied.

steps.what: Technician downloads satellite scenes and copies drone or aircraft files with their sensor and position data
Technician corrects skew and terrain distortion by orthorectifying images with ground control points
Technician corrects raw data for atmospheric variation such as haze and light conditions
Technician checks corrected images against check points in the accuracy report of the batch run
Technician compares corrected images with earlier imagery and judges clouds, shadows and errors
Technician writes the corrections and parameters used in the processing log

tasks.design: For satellite work the technician orders free satellite products that are already atmospherically corrected, so most of that correction step disappears. For drone and aircraft data a saved batch chain in the photogrammetry software orthorectifies with the surveyor's ground control points and runs atmospheric correction with set parameters per sensor, and writes an accuracy report and its parameters to the processing log. The technician checks residuals, clouds and shadows and decides what to redo. No learning model is used; every step is a fixed algorithm.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each scene was corrected step by step by hand, and parameters were copied into a log.
tasks.enabler_now: Free analysis-ready satellite data, and batch chains in photogrammetry software that log their parameters.
tasks.still_hard: Scenes with cloud, haze or steep terrain.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a correct-looking image is shifted against the real ground.
tasks.altitude: Less button pressing per scene; image acceptance stays with the technician.

reach.learn: Whether control point files in a fixed format cut rework in the batch chain.

evidence.claim: Copernicus offers free, atmospherically corrected Sentinel-2 data and mosaics.
Photogrammetry software runs orthorectification with control points in batch and reports residuals.

assumptions: Boundary: from raw data to corrected, logged images; analysis and maps are separate tasks.

Input contract for s2: ground control point coordinates measured by the land surveyor with a GNSS receiver and exported as a file in a fixed format; flight position data written by the drone or aircraft system; fallback is picking points by hand.

Input contract for s3: about 60% of projects use free satellite products corrected by the space programme's own processing; the rest run the saved chain with sensor parameters set by the technician; s3 is priced at that mix.
Input contract for s4 and s6: the processing software writes the parameters and accuracy report of each run to the log; the technician adds notes on redone scenes.
Checking keeps most of its time.

Pricing of s4: the batch run computes residuals at every check point and writes the accuracy report, replacing measuring check points by hand; the technician reads the report and inspects outliers, about 35% of the step.
s6 is the first record of corrections and parameters in the processing log and keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of satellite against drone and aircraft work.
research_questions: How often does the batch chain need a rerun by hand?

already_counted.description: Technician checks residual reports from batch runs.

incremental.description: Technician maintains the batch chains and sensor parameter sets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly new aircraft sensors with hand-tuned corrections; high: mostly work on free corrected satellite data and repeat drone flights with a stable chain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Load processed layers, write layer metadata, check for errors, develop or maintain geospatial information databases, answer data requests and archive old layers.

steps.what: Technician loads new processed layers into the geospatial database
Technician writes metadata for each layer: source, date, resolution and projection
Technician checks layers for topology, projection and attribute errors and fixes them
Technician develops the database structure for new project needs
Scientists and planners ask for layers or search the data catalogue
Technician answers data requests and sends layers
Technician archives superseded layers

tasks.design: An import script loads layers exported by the processing chain into the geospatial database with schema checks, and fills metadata fields from the image headers and the processing log, so the technician adds only a description. Validation rules flag topology, projection and attribute errors for the technician to fix. Colleagues find and download layers in a data catalogue linked to the database, and an archive rule moves superseded layers on a fixed schedule after the technician confirms. Designing the database stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layers were loaded and described one by one, and every request went by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Spatial databases with import scripts, validation rules and catalogues are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Structuring data for a project nobody has done before.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which layer a scientist really needs.
tasks.altitude: Less loading and mailing; database design stays with the technician.

reach.learn: Whether the catalogue answers most requests without mail.

evidence.claim: Spatial databases load layers by script, validate geometry and publish a searchable catalogue.
A grower in a Dutch precision farming trial found data tools not plug-and-play, so exchange formats need set-up work.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping the geospatial database current and usable; analysis is outside.

Input contract for s1: layers exported by the processing chain in the agreed format and naming; layers from outside parties in other formats are loaded by hand (about 30%); s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: image headers and the processing log written by the processing software; the technician writes the description.
Input contract for s6: colleagues search the catalogue themselves (s5) with about the effort of a mail request; layers with use limits are still sent by the technician.
Database design keeps its full time; colleagues' time is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: How many layers are added per month.
research_questions: How many requests still come by mail after the catalogue goes live?

incremental.description: Technician maintains import scripts, validation rules and catalogue entries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many outside layers in mixed formats; high: mostly own processed layers and many internal requests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have flight logs and control point files produced, maintain records of survey data in the survey register, file raw data and products, check for gaps and answer questions on what was flown when.

steps.what: Drone pilot completes the flight in the flight planning app, which writes the flight log
Technician copies flight details into the survey register: date, area, sensor, altitude and weather
Technician records the ground control and check points measured in the field
Technician files raw data and products in the project folders with the naming rules
Technician checks the register for missing records and files
Technician answers questions on which areas were flown when

tasks.design: The survey register becomes a small database. An import reads the flight log the drone's planning app writes after each flight, and the surveyor's GNSS export for control points, so the technician only checks them; contractor flight reports in PDF are still typed. From each register record a script creates the project folders and file names, and a completeness check lists flights with missing files or records. A map view of flight footprints answers most 'what was flown when' questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Flight details lived in app logs, field sheets and PDFs and were copied into a spreadsheet by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Flight planning apps and GNSS receivers export logs and point files in fixed formats.
tasks.still_hard: Contractor flights reported in free form.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a flight log does not match what the images show.
tasks.altitude: Less copying; the technician still owns the register.

reach.learn: Whether flight logs arrive complete enough to import.

evidence.claim: Flight planning apps and GNSS receivers export flight logs and point files that a register can import.
Per-user change logs in a register can monitor performance and need works council consent if used that way.

assumptions: Boundary: survey records from flight to filed data; processing is a separate task.

Input contract for s2: flight logs written by the drone's flight planning app after each flight (s1), with date, area, altitude and sensor; weather from the pilot's entry in the app; contractor flights (about 30%) come as PDF reports and are typed; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3: control point coordinates exported by the land surveyor's GNSS receiver in a fixed format; fallback is typing from the field sheet.
Input contract for s4 and s5: the register record from s2 drives folder names and the list of expected files; the technician maintains the scripts.
Pilot time is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: Flights per month and the share flown by contractors.
research_questions: How many register errors are found later in processing, before and after?

already_counted.description: Technician checks imported flight records that failed the import rules.

incremental.description: Technician maintains the import, folder and completeness scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many contractor flights reported in PDF; high: own drone flights with complete app logs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss the request with the scientist, check existing imagery, evaluate remote sensing project requirements to determine the equipment or software needed, write the proposal and have it approved.

steps.what: Technician discusses the project requirements with the scientist: area, image type, resolution and timing
Technician checks whether existing satellite, aerial or own imagery already covers the need
Technician looks up resolution, bands and costs of the team's sensors and software in the sensor sheet
Technician evaluates which sensors, platforms and software meet the requirements
Technician writes the equipment and software proposal with costs
Project lead approves the final proposal

tasks.design: Saved searches in the satellite data catalogue and a map of the team's own flight footprints show quickly whether existing imagery meets the area, date and resolution needed. A sheet of the team's sensors and software with resolution, bands, day rate and licence costs fills the cost table of the proposal template. Talking with the scientist, choosing the equipment and the lead's approval stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each request started with fresh catalogue searches and costs looked up again.
tasks.enabler_now: Satellite catalogues with saved area searches and the team's own flight register.
tasks.still_hard: Requirements the scientist cannot yet state.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which sensor will show what the scientist is after.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and costing; choices stay with the technician and the lead.

reach.learn: Whether standard cost tables make proposals easier to compare.

evidence.claim: Copernicus publishes free Sentinel-2 data and mosaics that can be searched by area.
No AI Act high-risk area covers choosing survey equipment.

assumptions: Boundary: from the request to the approved proposal; buying or hiring equipment is outside.
Input contract for s2: the satellite catalogue and the survey register's flight footprints kept by the technician; national aerial photos searched as today.
Input contract for s3 and s5: a sensor and cost sheet kept current by the technician; fallback is looking up rates.
The discussion and the choice keep their full or nearly full time; the lead's approval is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: Number of new projects per month.
research_questions: How often does existing imagery replace a new flight?

incremental.description: Technician keeps the sensor and cost sheet current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual projects with new sensors; high: repeat monitoring projects in known areas.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
